Instrument (EN): Patient Perspectives on Trauma-Informed Care Scale — refined 17-item US inpatient research version
Scales / measured domains (EN): Overall perceived trauma-informed care experience in physician-patient relationship. Five qualitative THEMES (listening; transparency; prior healthcare experiences; care coordination; attentiveness) are NOT independently validated scored subscales.
Research provenance: Pierre-Wright et al., Patient Educ Couns, online 2026-09-09, DOI 10.1016/j.pec.2026.109856, PMID42731200. 90 hospitalized adults (53% response); initial 20 items alpha=.90; removed 3 reverse-coded -> refined 17-item alpha=.91; correlation Trust in Physician Scale r=.64. Theme set came from qualitative interviews ~10% participants; factor structure unconfirmed.

Instrument (EN): Strategies for Trauma-Informed Care assessment — 24-item English service-provider practices form
Scales / measured domains (EN): One supported overall provider self-report factor / mean score. Content: Connecting (8 items), Empowering (8), Correcting (8), with six 4-item strategy groupings (Mindful Awareness; Engagement; Ecological; Physiological; Proactive; Responsive); theoretical domains, NOT validated separate scores.
Research provenance: Shelley LT, Becker Rázuri E, Shelashska R, Austin M, Knight D. J Public Child Welfare, online 2026-09-03, DOI10.1080/15548732.2026.2726254. Eight US TBRI practitioner trainings Feb2021–Jul2022: 1,109 eligible, 561 pretraining respondents consented, 509 with at least one relevant item, 313 posttraining respondents, n260 paired overall-change analysis. PCA/CFA favored ONE factor; self-reported practice improved after training.
DB locales: No STIC-TIC matching title/key in Master A:C3993, registered tab11 or live Supabase; explicitly DIFFERENT from existing Systemic Therapy Inventory of Change, STIC-Initial/STIC-Intersession entries.
EN form: EN-US administered RESPONDENT survey confirmed: methods explicitly state current study collected responses only in English. ORIGINAL US English research form; not a new translated version.

ES form: ES translation, psychometric validation, and scoring rights not verified.
Other translations: Other language respondent adaptations not independently documented in the primary paper.
Target population: US service providers in adoption/foster care, youth, mental health, counseling, education and other human services. TBRI trainee convenience sample; majority women, largely white; not general client symptom questionnaire.

Instrument (EN): Latin American Mental Health Scale — original 30-item occupational research edition
Scales / measured domains (EN): Four correlated factors: Anxiety (10), Stress (10), Subjective Well-being (7), Sleep Problems (3). Data-driven alternative model merges sleep-related items into Stress: 3 factors, not the same 4 separate clinical diagnoses.
Research provenance: Rosas-Carmona MJ, Jiménez S, Hernández-Moreno FP. Frontiers in Psychology 2026-06-10, DOI10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1823291. Initial occupational online validation N308, nonprobability multi-Latin-America sample 259 Mexico (84.1%), Colombia25, Peru7, Ecuador4, others. 4-factor CFA CFI=.933 RMSEA=.072; anxiety/stress alpha=.91, wellbeing alpha=.74, sleep alpha=.68. Alternative 3-factor EFA/CFA internal split n154+n154 same 308, not independent cohorts.
